title: Preserving an indexed segment
statement: Let $\mu,\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,N,p,\mathrm{top}$ be natural numbers, and let $l$ be a list of natural numbers of length $N$. Suppose its entries agree with $\mu(a+i)$ for $0\le i<N$ (after viewing each entry as an integer), every entry is less than $p$, and $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. If $\mu$ and $\mu'$ agree at every natural number $b$ satisfying $a\le b<a+N$ and $b<\mathrm{top}$, then the same list also has these properties as an indexed segment for $\mu'$, with the same $a,N,p,\mathrm{top}$.
hypotheses_covered: Agreement of $l$ with $\mu$ on the segment starting at $a$
Every entry of $l$ is less than $p$
Agreement of $\mu$ and $\mu'$ whenever $a\le b<a+N$ and $b<\mathrm{top}$
